summary: Traces the Bavarian Illuminati, Adam Weishaupt's 1776 Enlightenment secret society, into the master conspiracy theory, then follows Kerry Thornley, whose Discordian pranks revived it before his slide into paranoia and an attempt to molest a child.
keywords: Illuminati: New World Order card game

evidence.note: Weishaupt's birth in Ingolstadt opens the biography
Order founded on 1 May 1776, later renamed the Bavarian Illuminati
Weishaupt exiled to Regensburg, spends decades defending the order, dies around 1830
French Revolution blamed on the Illuminati; long segment on French women's Masonic lodges
1790s Illuminati panic in the young US, Washington and Abigail Adams
Thornley and Greg Hill introduced as 1950s Whittier teenagers
Possible MKUltra dosing of Thornley and Oswald at Atsugi base
Robert Welch and the John Birch Society adopt the Illuminati conspiracy
DA Jim Garrison investigates and charges Thornley from 1968
Account of Thornley trying to molest a young girl in Atlanta, discussed at length
Thornley's 1992 TV appearance and death in 1998
Alt-right meme culture and Kek traced to Discordian tactics, sets reaches_present

notes: Illuminati given org_type political-org as nearest fit for an Enlightenment secret society. Weishaupt kept secondary although parts 1-2 centre on him; Thornley is the bastard of parts 3-6. Transcript says Wilson died around 2003-04; real death year 2007 used. Prehistoric and Templar background excluded from covered_span; post-1998 alt-right epilogue sets reaches_present.
